out.rationale: Burns et al. ask how important errors in the weak supervision are and how different kinds of weak label biases affect generalisation. Lang, Sontag and Vijayaraghavan give error bounds based on expansion of the data distribution and student hypothesis class that capture pseudolabel correction and coverage expansion; they show the expansion properties can be checked from finite data and give empirical evidence that they hold in practice.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how weak-label errors affect the generalisation of a strong student trained on weak labels, via expansion-based learning theory

text: The authors show that existing weak supervision theory fails to account for two effects of weak-to-strong generalization: pseudolabel correction (the strong student corrects the weak teacher's errors) and coverage expansion (the student generalizes to examples where the teacher is not confident, even when these are excluded from training). They give new error bounds based on expansion properties of the data distribution and the student hypothesis class, capturing the intuition that weak-to-strong generalization occurs when the strong model cannot fit the teacher's mistakes without incurring additional error, and show the expansion properties can be checked from finite data, with empirical evidence that they hold.
title: Expansion bounds for weak-to-strong: pseudolabel correction and coverage expansion
